question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5z}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{10z}} & = \\ \frac{5z}{\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{10z}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z}}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z}} & = \\ \frac{5z(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z})}{(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{10z})(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z})} & = \\ \frac{5z(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z})}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}-(\sqrt{10z})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{5z(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z})}{2-10z} & = \\ \frac{5z(\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{10z})}{2(1-5z)}\end{aligned}
$$
